prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: Direct costs can include failing to provide useful information or perspectives on an issue, failing to support people seeking access to important resources, or failing to provide value by completing tasks with legitimate business uses.
DEMAND: Direct costs can include failing to provide useful information or perspectives on an issue, failing to support people seeking access to important resources, or failing to provide value by completing tasks with legitimate business uses
BEARER: direct costs

cli.result:
1. Direct costs may include failing to provide useful information or perspectives on an issue. This one failure alone can count as a direct cost.
2. Direct costs may include failing to support people seeking access to important resources. This one failure alone can count as a direct cost.
3. Direct costs may include failing to provide value by completing tasks with legitimate business uses. This one failure alone can count as a direct cost.
4. Direct costs may include any combination of the three failures, not just one at a time.
5. The three failures are only examples. Direct costs may also include other things not listed.
6. "Useful" applies to both "information" and "perspectives". Only failing to provide useful information, or useful perspectives, counts.
7. "Useful" applies only to "information". Failing to provide any perspectives on an issue, useful or not, counts.
8. "On an issue" applies to both "information" and "perspectives". Only failing to provide information or perspectives about an issue counts.
9. "On an issue" applies only to "perspectives". Failing to provide useful information of any kind, whether about an issue or not, counts.
10. "With legitimate business uses" describes the tasks. The failure that counts is not completing tasks that have legitimate business uses, and so not providing value.
11. "With legitimate business uses" describes the value. The failure that counts is not providing value with legitimate business uses by completing tasks.
